hints.title: Exponential Path Search Obstacle
hints.text: Exploring paths from every cell with naive recursion recomputes overlapping paths exponentially many times, timing out on large grids. Because each step in a path must strictly increase in cell value, why are cycles naturally impossible?

hints.title: Implicit DAG and Topological Order
hints.text: Because values strictly increase along any valid path, the grid forms a directed acyclic graph where cells can be processed in topological order without recursion depth concerns.

hints.title: In-Degree Calculation and Level-by-Level BFS
hints.text: Compute the in-degree of every cell, defined as the number of neighboring cells with strictly smaller values. Initialize a queue with all cells having zero in-degree. In each level of breadth-first search, increment the path length and decrement the in-degree of strictly larger neighbors, enqueueing any neighbor whose in-degree reaches zero.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

complexity.notes: Iterative topological sort (Kahn's BFS) on DAG formed by strictly increasing cell values.

solutions.approach: Iterative Topological Sort (Kahn's Algorithm on Grid DAG)
